_schema.one_file_per_subsection: section2.1_paragraph_ledger.json is THIS file (subsection 2.1). 2.2-2.5 get parallel files of the same schema, created one subsection at a time.
_schema.shape: paragraphs = fields (keyed P1..Pn). Each paragraph field has subfields: plan (intent/serves/boundary/thin_claim/guardrails) + propositions[] + prose_gate + final_prose.
_schema.the_gate_rule: final_prose stays EMPTY and prose_status = BLOCKED until EVERY proposition in that paragraph has verdict in {SUPPORTED} (or is explicitly downgraded AND user-approved). Only then write prose; show user (RULE 2); on approval write into thesis_draft.tex.
_schema.evidence_rule: The ONLY admissible evidence is VERBATIM cited_text recorded in proposition.verification.evidence[]. The model's prose ANSWER is recorded in answer_nonevidence for context but is NEVER admissible (E3.5).
workflow_loop_per_paragraph: 1. Lock the paragraph's propositions (statement + source + type).
2. For each external-NLM prop: run ONE atomized non-leading query (E3-E6) -> record verbatim cited_text -> set verdict.
3. For each legal-primary prop: fetch the OFFICIAL legal text (context-mode fetch, not raw WebFetch) -> record verbatim quote + exact reference -> set verdict.
4. When all verdicts SUPPORTED -> prose_gate.unlocked = true.
5. Draft final_prose to the thin-claim ceiling; show user (RULE 2).
6. On approval: prose_status = COMMITTED; write into thesis_draft.tex 2.1; advance current_paragraph.

P1.lit_body: disclosure-withholding theory + the MNPI/materiality legal setting
P1.intent: A firm privately committed to an acquisition but not yet announcing sits in a distinct DISCLOSURE STATE, not a balance-sheet state: the pending deal is material nonpublic information, yet the quarterly call -- especially unscripted Q&A -- is a standing obligation. The firm may stay silent but, once it speaks, may not mislead; so the CEO must host the call while unable to address the one material thing and unable to deny it. Disclosure theory frames a withholding state as informative; that bind is the paper's organizing primitive.
P1.serves: Installs 'disclosure state' as the lens; grounds it in disclosure theory + the legal setting; sets up the venue (P2) and the mechanism (P3).
P1.boundary: No mechanism yet (the deflection->hedging consequence is P3). No cash yet (P5). Do not define the measure (2.3).
P1.thin_claim: State the descriptive/correlational posture near the open. Materiality scoped to the acquirer (Basic = 'can be material', NOT 'every deal is MNPI').
guardrails: Do NOT assert a legal GAG. Frame: material (Basic) + nonpublic + may-stay-silent-but-not-mislead (Basic/10b-5). Keeps compliance-vs-strategic OPEN for P7.
Scope materiality to the ACQUIRER; a small bolt-on may be immaterial to a large acquirer.
Theory (Verrecchia/Dye) is the LENS that withholding states are informative; the legal cites establish THIS firm is in such a state. Do not conflate voluntary (theory) with compelled (legal).

Section 4 is devoted to an illustration of another class of disclosure  theories. There, I establish that it may be to the mutual benefit of both  managers and shareholders not to have managers disclose information  which investors know they have and which does not affect the firm's  earnings (exclusive of management compensation). verification.answer_nonevidence:
In Dye (1985), the decision of whether a manager discloses or withholds nonproprietary information is primarily determined by two theoretical frameworks: **the market's uncertainty regarding whether the manager has actually received information**, and **the potential for disclosure to disrupt principal-agent compensation contracts** [1-3].

**The Role of the Manager Being Uninformed**
The possibility that a manager might simply be uninformed plays a critical role in sustaining the non-disclosure of bad news. Under the standard "disclosure principle," if the market knows a manager has information, the manager is forced to disclose it to prevent investors from assuming the worst and driving the stock price down [4, 5]. However, this principle fails when investors are unsure if the manager actually has any news [1].

Because a manager **cannot credibly prove that they have not received new information**, investors observing silence cannot distinguish between a manager who is hiding bad news and a manager who genuinely has nothing to report [6]. Consequently, the market price of the firm in the event of no disclosure becomes a weighted average of the firm's unconditional expected value (if the manager is uninformed) and the expected value of the suppressed bad news [7]. 

This dynamic allows the manager to **rationally withhold any information whose actual value falls below this blended "no-disclosure" market price** [7]. As long as there is a probability that the manager is uninformed, they can hide bad news behind that possibility, meaning **a policy of complete, full disclosure is never an equilibrium** [8, 9]. 

**Contracting and Principal-Agent Determinants**
If investors *already know* that the manager possesses information, the decision to withhold it is determined by how its release would impact the manager's compensation contract [2]. 

In a firm where ownership and management are separated, a manager's unobservable effort is partly evaluated using the firm's market price, which aggregates the private information and forecasts of various investors [10, 11]. If the manager discloses their private information early, that announcement dominates and completely determines the trajectory of the firm's stock price [10]. Doing so effectively **destroys the other information contained in the market price that is useful for contracting purposes** (i.e., information that helps owners accurately gauge the manager's effort) [12, 13]. 

Therefore, in this scenario, **managers withhold information because doing so preserves the informational value of the stock price for their compensation contracts** [12, 14]. Selective or complete non-disclosure can actually be mutually beneficial to both shareholders and managers, as unselective disclosure might produce better earnings forecasts but inferior measures of the manager's actual performance [13, 15].

propositions.role_in_paragraph: Establishes that the pending (undisclosed) deal is MATERIAL -> combined with 'nonpublic' (definitional) it is MNPI. Anchors the disclosure-state premise in law.

propositions.statement: A firm has no general affirmative duty to disclose confidential merger negotiations (silence is permitted), but once it speaks it may not mislead -- an untrue or half-true statement is unlawful. So denial is not a lawful option, leaving deflection.
propositions.role_in_paragraph: Completes the BIND: explains why the CEO cannot simply deny and move on. The deflection->hedging CONSEQUENCE is developed in P3 (handoff).

P2.lit_body: earnings calls as a disclosure venue + textual analysis of call language
P2.intent: The earnings call is where the bind becomes legible: a recurring, semi-spontaneous event whose unscripted Q&A is far less managed than prepared remarks, and a large literature shows call LANGUAGE carries information beyond the numbers. Reading it quantitatively -- word-classification dictionaries, the presentation/Q&A split -- is an established method this paper adopts and extends to a dimension prior work has not read: uncertainty.
P2.serves: Situates the measurement venue + call-textual-analysis literature; establishes unscripted call language is informative; names the presentation/Q&A split the design rests on.
P2.boundary: Do not construct the residual (2.3). Venue + reading-method + informativeness only.
P2.thin_claim: Adopt-and-extend; no claim prior measures captured uncertainty.

propositions.role_in_paragraph: Licenses reading Q&A language as a signal.

propositions.statement: Word-classification dictionaries built for financial text measure tone/uncertainty, and these linguistic features are informative.
propositions.role_in_paragraph: Licenses the dictionary method for the uncertainty read.

propositions.statement: Linguistic features of disclosure (e.g., complexity/readability) carry information beyond the numbers.

P3.lit_body: the mechanism -> ANTICIPATORY dimension (incl. strategic silence)
P3.intent: Under the bind, the CEO cannot answer the forbidden question directly, so unscripted answers turn hedged, qualified, non-committal -- uncertainty language rises in the Q&A. Keyed to the undisclosed state, the rise is present while the deal is secret and resolves once announcement makes it public (the information clock).
P3.serves: Derives the ANTICIPATORY dimension (timing -> H1, H1b); justifies reading uncertainty WORDS not silence.
P3.boundary: Conceptual signal only; the residual measure is 2.3.
P3.thin_claim: A pattern keyed to the disclosure state -- no causal claim about CEO intent.

propositions.role_in_paragraph: Grounds the deflection mechanism in the call-silence literature.

P4.lit_body: managerial style / manager fixed effects -> why the signal is the call-varying component
P4.intent: Call-language uncertainty is partly a CEO's persistent style: managers differ durably in how they speak, and style is a fixed trait, not an anticipatory signal. An anticipatory, deal-tracking component must appear and disappear within one executive's tenure -> it can only live in the call-VARYING part, once persistent style is netted out. This is why the paper works with a within-CEO, call-level component.
P4.serves: Reviews managerial-style literature; makes the conceptual case the signal must be the call-varying component (what 2.3's residual operationalizes).
P4.boundary: CONCEPTUAL only -- do NOT write eq-4 or list first-stage regressors (2.3).

propositions.statement: Managers have persistent, individual styles that load as manager fixed effects in firm policies/outcomes -- a measurable, durable manager-specific component.
propositions.role_in_paragraph: Grounds 'persistent style must be netted out'.

P5.lit_body: corporate cash holdings + cash-for-acquisitions -> CASH-CONCENTRATED dimension
P5.intent: Cash and stock deals differ in one design-relevant way: a cash purchase requires an accumulated, visible balance-sheet position -- a war chest -- while a stock deal carries the identical disclosure setting with no comparable visible cash commitment. That makes stock the placebo and a cash-CONCENTRATED signal informative on its own; WHY cash differs is left open. The two clocks then diverge: uncertainty tracks the information and resolves at announcement, while the cash position serves the purchase and -- mechanically -- persists until paid at completion.
P5.serves: Reviews cash-holdings literature; sets up CASH as a DESIGN CONTRAST (-> H1a) + the stock placebo (-> MA3); frames differential-timing CONTRAST (-> H1b), cash-persistence leg labeled mechanical.
P5.boundary: Do NOT assert 'cash sharpens the bind / visible cash invites the question' -- that IS the scrutiny channel 4.1 rules out. DESIGN CONTRAST only. Concentration, NOT strict specificity. Keep cash CENTRAL.
P5.thin_claim: A where-it-appears CONTRAST; the why stays open; the cash-persistence leg is mechanical.
